title: I Used the IKEA As-Is Return Window on the Clerk Who Marked It Final

parts.text: I carried the dented Billy back at 11:02 a.m. inside the 90-day as-is window printed on the yellow tag. The clerk who had marked FINAL SALE yesterday was on returns. The as-is card at the desk said: AS-IS RETURNS WITHIN 90 DAYS WITH TAG. I was thirty-eight, apartment renter, holding the tag and the receipt. Clerk Bo said, "Yellow means goodbye." I pointed at the card. He tapped FINAL. "Warehouse language." I photographed the tag dates, the card, and his mark. Then I used the kiosk return with the same SKU. At 11:08 the returns lead asked why Bo's mark was on a window-denial ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The returns lead can see a 90-day tag against a FINAL mark Bo added.

social.video_title: He stamped FINAL on a 90-day as-is tag — Part 1/2
social.description: Dented Billy, a yellow tag still in window, and warehouse language. I used the kiosk. Would you have kept the dent?

parts.text: Bo called it a training stamp until the kiosk refund posted. I printed the ticket, the card, and the photo. Billy went back. Bo told the break room the card was always about optics. Optics is a word clerks use when a kiosk exists. As-is policy now has a second line: YELLOW IS NOT GOODBYE INSIDE 90. I have floor space. Bo retrains stamps. The warehouse finally reads the tag.

social.video_title: Yellow is not goodbye inside 90 — Part 2/2
social.description: Window-denial ticket, a kiosk refund, and a second line on the card. Was warehouse language ever a stamp?
